purpose: Heap budgets of puae6.wbx and the classification of its memory (T19b), with the measurements they come from (`measured` for the A500, `measured_a600` for the A600, `measured_a1200` for the A1200: the three fit the same budgets, T23e, T24f; `measured_<machine>_<memory>` for a configuration with other memory, T49, whose mmap budget follows `memory_budget`). The layout is what the harness and the BizHawk wrapper give Waterbox when they create the sandbox. The classification follows the table of docs/03-waterbox.md: nothing is excluded from the snapshot, every mutable byte is captured by default.

budget_basis.rule: A budget is at least twice the largest committed size measured (sbrk, mmap) or the structural worst case (sealed), in whole MiB; heaps the guest does not use stay at one 16 KiB host page, the smallest the runtime accepts. tests/waterbox-smoke/test_puae6.py fails when a measurement exceeds half of its budget, so a change that grows the machine has to revisit this file.
budget_basis.sbrk: musl's brk heap: only small allocations land here (measured 16 KiB). 4 MiB leaves room for the bridge and a growing option set.
budget_basis.sealed: The firmware and every medium are copied here during p6w_init and frozen by the seal: a 512 KiB Kickstart plus P6_MAX_MEDIA (16) ADF images of 901120 bytes is 14 942 208 bytes; 16 MiB holds it. The micro-ROM fixture uses 256 KiB.
budget_basis.invisible: Nothing calls alloc_invisible: no state is excluded from the snapshot. The smallest heap the runtime accepts.
budget_basis.plain: Nothing calls alloc_plain: everything mutable is ordinary malloc or static data, which Waterbox captures. The smallest heap the runtime accepts.
budget_basis.mmap: Large malloc blocks, Chip and Slow RAM among them (measured 5.3 MiB on the A500, 4.8 MiB on the A600, whose 1 MiB of Chip RAM replaces 512 KiB of Chip and 512 KiB of Slow RAM and which has no Slow RAM block to allocate, and 5.8 MiB on the A1200, whose 2 MiB of Chip RAM and AGA tables are the largest). 16 MiB is 2.7 times the largest (A1200, T24f: twice 5.8 MiB is 11.6 MiB, so the half rule holds with 4.4 MiB of room): one budget serves the three machines. The AGA code (+9.8 MB, T24b) lives in the elf region, which is not a budgeted heap.

memory_budget.rule: mmap heap of a configuration = layout.mmap + mmap_extra_factor * extra memory, where the extra memory is the Fast RAM in full plus the Chip and Slow RAM above what the machine comes with (A500 512 KiB Chip + 512 KiB Slow, A600 1 MiB Chip, A1200 2 MiB Chip). The other heaps do not change. A configuration with no extra memory keeps the base layout, so the snapshot, the identity and every measurement of the stock machines are what they were.
memory_budget.why: The base rule of budget_basis is a budget of at least twice what was measured. Fast RAM is allocated at load from the mmap heap (an 8 MiB board added 8 396 800 bytes to the committed size of the A1200, board and bookkeeping), so the budget grows by twice the memory asked for and the half rule keeps holding: A1200 + 8 MiB Fast committed 14 499 840 of a 33 554 432 budget, the A1200 with 1.5 MiB Slow and 8 MiB Fast 16 613 376 of 36 700 160. The wrapper computes the same budget (Puae6Core.Heaps(settings)) and tests/waterbox-state compares the two.
memory_budget.dirty_pages: A board is cleared at power-on without writing the zeros it already holds (patch 0114): its pages stay clean until the guest writes them, so the snapshot after 60 units of an A1200 with 8 MiB of Fast RAM is 10 309 076 bytes against 10 186 196 without the board (before the patch it was 18 714 068, every page of the board dirty).
memory_budget.floppy_writes: A core created with the sync setting FloppyWrites (P6_CONFIG_FLOPPY_WRITES, T28) reserves the write overlay at load: a pool of 3520 sectors and 16 raw tracks, about 2 MiB, allocated from the mmap heap. The wrapper counts it as 4096 KiB of extra memory (Puae6Core.FloppyOverlayKiB), so the mmap heap of such a core is layout.mmap + mmap_extra_factor * 4096 KiB more than the base, plus whatever extra memory the machine asks for. measured_a500_floppy_writes_full is the worst case: a guest that rewrites every track of both disks (tests/waterbox-media/wb12.py, 3520 sectors) committed 3.9 MiB more in the mmap heap than the stock machine (9 502 720 against 5 586 944 bytes) and its snapshot is 1.9 MiB bigger; the budget is more than twice the committed size.
memory_budget.hard_file: A hard file (P6_MEDIA_HDF, T29d) is extra memory of the mmap heap like Fast RAM: the blob store keeps the base (the size of the image) and reserves beside it, at p6_load, the room for the overlay of the guest's writes (the size of the image again, 4 KiB chunks made on first write) and its dirty bitmap, so the heap asks for hard_file_copies x the image + the bitmap (1 bit per 4 KiB chunk) + hard_file_allocator_kib KiB, which is HardFileHeapKiB in the smoke (the counterpart of MacHawk's HardDiskHeapKB, which has one copy: its writes go in place) and counts twice in the budget like all extra memory. The image is NOT copied into the sealed heap (p6w_init gives p6_load the host's buffer), so the sealed heap stays at the firmware. Measured with the micro-ROM that writes a chunk a unit (tests/hdf/hdf_rom.py, loop_program): measured_a500_hdf2048 (2 MiB image) commits 9 814 016 bytes of mmap against 5 586 944 of the A500 without a hard file (+4 227 072 = twice the image + 32 768) and measured_a500_hdf32768 (32 MiB) 72 728 576 (twice the image + 5 619 712): the half rule holds by construction (2 x (2 I + C) <= 16 MiB + 4 I + 0.12 MiB as long as C, the machine, is under 8 MiB). What a snapshot carries does not follow the image: 9 797 876 bytes at unit 60 with 2 MiB and 9 859 324 with 32 MiB (the base is allocated before the seal, so it is the baseline of the snapshot, and only the dirty pages of the overlay and of the machine travel); the plain A500 (the boot micro-ROM, no hard file) is 9 203 892.

classification.region: image code and read-only data (RX and R segments of the ELF)
classification.treatment: Never written: the runtime maps them read-only, the snapshot does not carry them.

classification.region: image writable data and bss (RW segments of the ELF: the engine's globals, its tables, the picture and audio buffers)
classification.treatment: Captured by default as dirty pages. It mixes emulated state, algorithm state (Paula's filter, the blitter and drawing history) and derived caches; none of it is split out or excluded until a poison test exists (see candidates_for_exclusion).

classification.region: mmap heap (malloc of large blocks: Chip RAM, Slow RAM, engine tables)
sealed heap (copies of the firmware and of the media)
classification.treatment: Filled by p6w_init before the seal, read-only after it; the firmware and the ADF images are never patched. The bridge keeps pointers into it, never into host memory.
Empty: nothing is allocated from it, so nothing is excluded from the snapshot.
Empty: nothing is allocated from it.

classification.region: main and alternate thread stacks (runtime-owned, 1 MiB each)
classification.treatment: Empty at a unit boundary: p6_run_frame returns through the stack, there is no coroutine or continuation. The runtime does not put them in the snapshot.

classification.region: host buffers of a call (p6w_init, firmware and media as given, p6_input, p6w_frame)
classification.treatment: Host memory valid only during the call; the guest copies what it keeps. The harness overwrites them with 0xA5 after every call and the machine must not notice.

classification.region: video and audio returned by p6w_frame_advance
classification.treatment: Guest memory (the engine's picture and the bridge's audio queue), valid until the next call; the host reads it right after the call and keeps no pointer. Captured like the rest of the image.
None in this harness. The BizHawk wrapper (T20) inventories its own: buttons, selected disk, latched input.

candidates_for_exclusion.why: the engine's chunky picture buffer, written every unit
candidates_for_exclusion.needed: a poison test over both fields and mode changes before it can leave the snapshot (docs/03-waterbox.md); T36

candidates_for_exclusion.why: tables that are clean right after the seal and dirty after the first unit: the machine's reset head runs inside that unit, not inside p6_load
candidates_for_exclusion.needed: either run that head before the seal (without consuming a unit) or prove the tables rebuildable; T36
